feed.title: NPR Topics: Climate
feed.subtitle: In-depth coverage of climate change, weather events, climate science, emissions targets and adaptation strategies from NPR’s climate reporters.

entry.title: Oil giant ExxonMobil left Venezuela years ago. Now it's considering a return
entry.summary: ExxonMobil has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Venezuelan government and its state-owned oil company to explore opportunities in the country.

entry.title: Turkey hosts world climate summit, but some critics accuse it of 'greenwashing'
entry.summary: Thousands of diplomats, executives and leaders are gathering in Turkey for a global climate summit. In recent years, Turkey has moved to be more eco-conscious, but some say that hasn't been enough.

entry.title: U.N. climate talks begin today. Here are 3 things to know
entry.summary: Countries are gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual U.N. climate conference. Many are frustrated with the lack of focus on fossil fuels, the main driver of climate change.

entry.title: COP31 starts Monday. As global temperatures continue to rise, do climate talks matter?
entry.summary: COP31 - the annual UN negotiations on climate change - starts on Monday. The talks have been going on for decades, during which the planet has gotten hotter. So, do these climate talks really matter?

entry.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
entry.summary: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.

entry.title: In California, some towns are already dealing with impacts from El Niño
entry.summary: What could be the effects of an extreme El Nino this winter on California, and how are towns preparing?

entry.title: After last year's storm, this remote Alaska town is still picking up the pieces
entry.summary: In October 2025, the remnants of a typhoon seriously damaged Alaska Native villages in the far western part of the state. A year later, one of the hardest hit communities is still recovering.

entry.title: Halloween temperatures have been trending hotter. Here's what the data shows
entry.summary: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.

entry.title: Arizona's lifeline to the Colorado River is drying up. Its designers warned us decades ago
entry.summary: Arizona has now joined a lawsuit against the Trump administration's plan for sharing the Colorado River. But history shows water planners there saw big cuts to their water supply coming.

entry.title: Forecasters are predicting a warmer and wetter winter. Here's how El Niño will affect your region
entry.summary: El Niño years typically lead to more precipitation and higher-than-average temperatures. The latest data shows the different potential impacts by region.
